OOS_protocol.data_window: to be fixed in the registration before any data is read
OOS_protocol.train_test_boundary: last 30% of the PIT history plus walk-forward folds; universe membership frozen as of each fold's train end

capacity_model.note: set by the thinnest leg's depth; not measured in this repo

counterparty: perpetual longs in the top-funding asset (pay) and shorts in the bottom-funding asset (pay); the price leg is the risk premium, not a counterparty
drawdown_model: to be measured on price+funding P&L; funding-only drawdown is not a drawdown
economic_mechanism: Counterparty: leveraged longs in the high-funding perp pay shorts; long side receives from shorts in the low/negative-funding perp. Might persist because leverage demand is crowded and arbitrage capital is limited and sized by margin; might vanish when capital flows to the spread, when the high-funding asset's price rallies against the short leg (the funding is compensation for that risk, not free), or when delisting/illiquidity hits the extreme-funding names (survivorship hides that).
eligibility_rules: symbol active at decision time per the PIT universe
minimum 30d listing age and a stated minimum open interest
entry: at each rebalance, rank by trailing mean funding (read via asof(previous settlement)); short top-k, long bottom-k, dollar-neutral
execution_model: taker both legs, perp only; price-leg residual risk measured, not assumed away
exit: next rebalance or when the rank gap falls below a registered threshold
holding_period: 1 to 9 settlements (registered grid; every grid cell counts as a tested variant)
hypothesis: Across a point-in-time universe of perpetuals, the assets with the highest trailing funding keep paying more than the lowest, so short-high/long-low earns a funding spread net of costs.
prospective_protocol: register parameters and universe rule, then observe forward settlements via the trial journal; no parameter change during observation
rejection_conditions: adjusted p-value (Holm over every attempted variant) above 0.05 on historical_test or oos_test
net edge after assumed costs not positive
universe cannot be shown point-in-time (survivors only)
result depends on one symbol or one regime window
price-leg P&L over the sample is negative or larger in magnitude than the funding spread earned

required_data.gap: repo has only BTC/ETH/SOL Binance funding (hand-picked survivors); no delisted symbols
required_data.name: point-in-time perp listing/delisting records for the whole venue, including delisted symbols
funding history per symbol, 8h, all listed symbols

required_data.gap: mark_price column is blank for early history (e.g. BTC 2019) and is not a hedge-grade price series
required_data.name: mark/index price per symbol to hedge or measure the price legs
depth/spread per symbol for capacity and slippage

risk_model: unhedged cross-asset price spread between the two legs: beta/idiosyncratic move can exceed funding by orders of magnitude; liquidation of the short leg in a squeeze
status_note: SPECIFICATION ONLY. Nothing has been tested; this is not a winner. A bias_declaration is True only where the data needed to rule that bias out is in the repo; it is False wherever a required_data item with repo_has=false names it in declaration_keys. Such a candidate is not yet a testable specification (the verdict reports BIAS_NOT_RULED_OUT) until that data is collected.
